ambientCG is unreachable from the dev container (35/35 candidates failed

shortlist-results.json) and the round trip has to go through CI. Per
Jafar 2026-09-15: 'the round trip costs the same carrying one candidate

SAID PLAINLY: EVERY ID BELOW WAS CHOSEN FROM catalogue.json METADATA
ALONE -- an asset id, a size list, a download link, nothing else. No
image has been seen from this container (ambientcg.com and
api.polyhaven.com both confirmed blocked, 2026-09-15) or by the agent
that wrote this file. The CATEGORY choice per surface is reasoned (below);
the ID choice within a category is NOT -- ambientCG ids are sequential by
upload order, not by finish or condition, and carry no tag this
catalogue records. Going near-exhaustive within a category is what
removes that blindness instead of asking a spread to get lucky: every id
in the reasoned category is included, so the contact sheet after this
run has already seen everything worth seeing and the choice needs no
second CI round trip.
KERB -> ALL 67 Rock ids, not Concrete. The Hook sheet
(production/art/atlas-01/concepts/hook.png, origin/art/atlas-01) names
the material QUAY STONE and shows a heavily weathered, mottled
grey-green stone block, not cast concrete; queue 300 independently
condemns Concrete034 as 'the wrong material identity... quite apart from
being too pale'. fetch_textures.py already lists Rock as kerb's second
search term. 'Rocks001-025' (plural) is a separate ambientCG category --
excluded, not folded in blind: it reads as loose/scattered stone rather
than a dressed block, and if the Rock set comes back wrong that is the
next place to look, named rather than silently added now.
METAL -> ALL 100 Metal ids (strict 'Metal###', Metal032 the current pick
excluded), not MetalPlates or MetalWalkway. The Hook sheet's GALVANISED
DUSTBIN swatch is grey-silver, matte, corrugated sheet, with rust streak
staining -- not shiny, not solid rust, not a tread pattern. MetalPlates
(20 ids, diamond-plate tread) and MetalWalkway (14 ids, perforated
grate) are distinct ambientCG categories by their own taxonomy, not just
a naming accident, and a dustbin or bollard skin is not diamond-plate or
grating -- excluded on that category-level reasoning, which is different
in kind from the ID-level blindness above and is not being reconsidered
by this widening.
PLASTER -> all 5 untried ids, unchanged from the first pass. Only 7
Plaster ids exist in the whole catalogue; Plaster001 and Plaster002 are
already committed (plaster, plaster_b). This was already exhaustive.
CONCRETE -> ALL 58 remaining Concrete ids (Concrete017 current,
Concrete034 kerb's current, Concrete042A already committed as
concrete_b, excluded). Concrete is the LARGEST surface in the street
(150 pieces) with only 9.3 lumSD in it; the ask is more visible
aggregate and staining, not just a higher number -- Jafar's instruction
that a higher lumSD which is still a uniform wash has not fixed anything
applies hardest here, which is the argument for exhaustive over spread:
a spread could easily land on ten different flat cards.
SIZE, SO THE ROUND TRIP CAN BE PRICED BEFORE IT IS SPENT: 230 candidates
at 1K-JPG. Every id below was checked against the committed catalogue and
publishes both 1K-JPG (this pass) and 2K-JPG (what choices.json would
need for the final pick) -- zero network cost to confirm that, the whole
payoff of pulling the catalogue once.
NOT SHORTLISTED, AND WHY: PavingStones (155 ids) was considered for kerb
-- ambientCG's paving textures are jointed/patterned (multiple stones,
grout lines), which is the sidewalk's own material (PavingStones067) and
not a continuous kerb edge, so it was set aside rather than included
blind. If the Rock set reads wrong in the contact sheet, PavingStones is
the next place to look, not a second guess at Rock.
SETTS, ADDED 2026-09-21 for the promise made to Jafar that the free
library already on the allowlist carries cut setts or cobbles. ALL 148
PavingStones ids in this repo's committed catalogue.json snapshot (the
KERB note above recorded 155 live on ambientCG on 2026-09-15; today's
snapshot has fewer, unreconciled, and the live count is unchecked from
this container in any case, re-verified only when the fetch itself
runs). PavingStones is the RIGHT category here for the reason it was
EXCLUDED from kerb above: ambientCG's paving textures are jointed and
patterned, multiple stones with grout lines, which is wrong for a
continuous kerb edge and is exactly what a cut sett or cobble surface
is. No 'Cobblestone' or 'Sett' category exists in ambientCG's own
taxonomy (every prefix in catalogue.json checked, 2026-09-21); both
live inside PavingStones. Near-exhaustive for the same reason as KERB
and METAL: no image is visible from this container and the catalogue
carries no tag, so the blindness is at the id level only and is
removed by including the category whole rather than asking a spread
to get lucky. External confirmation only, since ambientcg.com is
confirmed unreachable from this container again today (403, agent
proxy log): PavingStones065 and PavingStones057 are described
elsewhere as small paving stones inspired by the cobblestones of
Prague; PavingStones150 is tagged Cobble and Cobblestone. THE PICK
CRITERION FOR THE CONTACT SHEET WHEN IT LANDS: British, not generic
European. Canon wants a wet northern port town's rectangular dressed
granite block, blue-grey to black, not the small rounded warm-toned
stone the Prague description implies -- overrule rank order by looking,
the same way the kerb pick was overruled by the Hook sheet's own QUAY
STONE swatch rather than taken by name. NOT YET A LOGICAL SURFACE:
AssetLibrary.cs (ledger/Assets/Scripts/Game/AssetLibrary.cs) declares
no Setts constant beside its Asphalt/Sidewalk/Kerb ones, and
pack_check.py's SURFACES list, deliberately hand-copied rather than
parsed from the C#, does not include 'setts' either. Landing this at
full resolution via choices.json fills the library gap but does not
by itself put the texture on anything the game draws; that needs a
small code change this fetch does not make, named in the fetch
record beside it rather than done here.
